title: Comparing Security-Framing vs. Innovation-Framing in National AISI Outputs: A Corpus Study

original_idea.body:
# Comparing Security-Framing vs. Innovation-Framing in National AISI Outputs: A Corpus Study

**Problem:** The subfield context flags a surprising divergence — UK AISI rebranded to 'AI Security Institute' (security framing) while US AISI became CAISI (innovation framing) — and asks whether framing affects safety outcomes, but this hasn't been studied empirically through what each institute actually publishes.

**Direction:** Assemble a corpus of public outputs from both institutes (and 1-2 others), and use a simple, pre-registered text-analysis pipeline (keyword/frame frequency, topic modeling, LLM-assisted frame labeling) to quantify how much each emphasizes security/risk vs. innovation/capability framing over time. Test whether the rebrands coincide with measurable shifts.

**Why it matters:** Empirically grounds a high-level strategic question about divergent national approaches to AI safety institutions — pure public-document analysis with strong counterfactual value. No lab access, light compute.

**Relevant context:** Extends the subfield's 'Recent Surprising Results' on UK AISI vs. US CAISI framing divergence, operationalizing the suggested follow-up via corpus analysis of institute publications.
